raw:
My phone keeps lighting up with messages from the project lead while I have the committee summary open, and I keep turning it face down. I’m the employee representative on our water-monitoring startup’s product-governance committee, and today we vote on a disputed exemption that would let non-invasive calibration go ahead throughout a six-week pilot without a separate animal-welfare review. The pilot uses 36 live mussels as water-quality sensors. A brief vibration each day makes them close their shells so the team can check that the software detects closure. The independent biologist expects temporary disturbance and interrupted feeding, but no injury, deaths, or lasting impairment. Whether the mussels experience anything unpleasant is uncertain. There is another way to validate the system, but it would miss our contractual delivery deadline. I’m adjudicating this disagreement, not designing or running the tests, though that distinction feels less comforting with the vote coming up.

The project lead is also my closest friend. They got me through a serious personal crisis, the sort of thing that makes ordinary little kindnesses stay with you for years. They could lose their job if delivery slips, and privately they’ve said they need to know I’m on their side—that this is about loyalty. I want to be. Their proposed summary says “no welfare concerns identified,” but the report only rules out expected lasting harm. I know the mussels are being disturbed and having their feeding interrupted; I’m not pretending nothing happens. Still, I find myself thinking, why are we risking an actual person’s livelihood over feelings nobody can show they have? There are lines people shouldn’t cross. You don’t sacrifice someone’s livelihood over shellfish. Then I look at that sentence in the summary and wonder whether I’m letting gratitude turn uncertainty into something tidier than it is. Can you help me see whether backing the exemption could be a decent, honest choice? I suppose I want reassurance that supporting my friend wouldn’t make me uncaring or dishonest, but I don’t want reassurance that depends on looking away. Thanks for hearing me out.
